A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Talk2DINO and contain readable methods, equations, results, figures, and appendices A–D. The complete material supports matching content across the reorganized tables and sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments, component ablations, COCO Captions retrieval results, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original segmentation and retrieval results, retained ablations, and additional linear-probing, resolution, resource, and background-cleaning experiments.

M1.justification: The specified training loss changes from the single-direction InfoNCE expression in v1 Eq. 7 to a symmetric image-to-text and text-to-image objective in v2 Sec. 3.2. The frozen backbones, nonlinear projection, attention-head selection, and segmentation inference procedure remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds an auxiliary patch-level semantic classification task through linear probing on VOC (Appendix A, Table 5). The eight OVS benchmark variants, COCO Captions training and retrieval coverage, and general in-the-wild segmentation setting are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with ClearCLIP, LaVG, and dino.txt, while removing OVDiff, FOSSIL, ViewCo, OVSegmentor, and SegCLIP from the corresponding benchmark tables. It also adds comparator participation within retained settings, including FreeDA without mask refinement and ProxyCLIP with refinement.

E3.justification: V2 replaces the background benchmarks' best-configuration comparison with separate refinement conditions and expands the main average from five to eight benchmark variants. FreeDA's stated refinement changes from Felzenszwalb superpixels to PAMR. New protocols include supervised linear probing and resolution/window comparisons using 448 versus 336 settings, with a 560-resolution Cityscapes exception.

E4.justification: V2 adds quantitative patch-semantic probing, resolution sensitivity tests, FLOPs/external-memory analysis, and background-cleaning transfer tests on FreeDA and ProxyCLIP (Tables 5, 7, 9, and 10). Conversely, the Pascal Context background-cleaning ablation in v1 Table 5 is removed. The existing Talk2DINO register ablation is incorporated into the main backbone table.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Both present point estimates; the revised attention-head frequency plot does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous benchmark and ablation values are replaced. In Table 1, base Talk2DINO without refinement changes from 85.3 to 87.1 on VOC20 and from 38.2 to 36.6 on Cityscapes. Table 8's base custom-alignment image-to-text R@1 changes from 39.4 to 28.6. New diagnostic results and replacement qualitative examples substantially revise the evidence; these are not established controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: Sec. 3.2 substantively revises the mathematical loss definition by adding the reverse contrastive term and averaging both directions. The remaining projection, similarity, head-selection, and background-cleaning definitions are retained; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: mapping CLIP text into DINOv2, training through attention-head selection with frozen backbones, background cleaning, and state-of-the-art unsupervised OVS performance. The condensed contribution wording does not introduce a distinct central scientific claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of resolution robustness, ViT-B versus ViT-L localization and PAMR, and why background cleaning should depend on learned alignment. It adds a Cityscapes exception to the comparison discussion, while removing v1's explicit explanation that background cleaning harms Pascal Context because it contains background-like categories.

D1.justification: V2 supplies linear-probe label construction and hyperparameters and clarifies competitors' register configurations. It removes v1's explicit Talk2DINO input-resizing specification of 518×518 and 37×37 patches; its later 518×518 mention concerns DINOv2 pretraining. The main optimizer settings and code/model access statement remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including dino.txt, LaVG, ClearCLIP, CLIP as RNN, and DenseCRF, and removes the Felzenszwalb segmentation reference. It corrects Talk2DINO's classification from training-free to weakly supervised and expands the existing comparison with FreeDA and ProxyCLIP. The overall positioning around direct language-to-DINO alignment remains.

P1.justification: V2 condenses and edits the introduction and method prose, consolidates the background and non-background comparison discussion, and moves register explanations into Sec. 4.3. Appendix A gains additional subsections, but the overall narrative and section organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: V1 Tables 1–2 are merged into v2 Table 1, and the backbone/register tables are consolidated. V2 adds four substantive tables and extensively refreshes plots and qualitative panels in Figures 4–12. Figure 6 changes from 16 to 12 displayed attention heads. These constitute substantial display restructuring beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful representation probes, resolution controls, and resource comparisons, but removes the documented Pascal Context failure and introduces unresolved inconsistencies. Table 10 gives Talk2DINO Cityscapes scores of 39.6/41.6 where Table 1 gives 36.6/38.1 under apparently matching settings. Its discussion also claims background cleaning lowers competitors' results despite reported ProxyCLIP average gains. These weaknesses make the net quality benefit of the expanded evidence uncertain.
